speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing any muscle stiffness, tremors, or a feeling that your limbs are moving involuntarily? I need to determine if these are signs of an extrapyramidal side effect from the risperidone.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to rule out other causes. Have you experienced any muscle rigidity, tremors at rest, or involuntary facial movements such as grimacing or tongue protrusion?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To further evaluate for other extrapyramidal symptoms, do you have any difficulty swallowing, excessive drooling, or a mask-like facial expression? I also need to know if you have noticed any slow, writhing movements of your hands or feet, or if your movements are quick and jerky.
